source.title: Diminishing Returns in Expanding Generative Models and Godel-Tarski-Lob Limits

record.tranche_reason: The paper is read in full and gives a formal result about marginal gains in solved-task coverage, but it neither tests nor relies on held-out language-model loss scaling or the compute-optimal allocation claim. Its scaling-law references are background citations.
record.gate_note: The paper cites the Kaplan and Hoffmann scaling-law papers and says its framework complements empirical scaling analyses, but reports no results from those studies and does not measure held-out cross-entropy, parameter/token/compute scaling, extrapolation, architecture effects, or downstream performance. Its own theorem concerns probability mass of newly solvable tasks under specified structural assumptions; record that related but different construct under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: Purely theoretical paper: it proves that marginal gains in solved-task probability mass vanish for nested systems under a fixed task distribution. It also proves a complexity-prior tail bound for prediction risk and logical incompleteness limits. It reports no models, no held-out loss, no power-law fits, no compute allocation and no downstream measurements. Kaplan and Hoffmann are cited only as background, so no claim version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that under a fixed task distribution and capability preservation, marginal gains in solved-task mass converge to zero. They add a prediction-theoretic bound via complexity-prior tail mass. They argue that Rosser, Tarski and Löb results imply persistent unresolved logical tasks. They frame this as complementing empirical scaling analyses, not testing them.
record.recipe_differences: The paper develops an abstract task-space framework and mathematical theorems rather than applying the original empirical loss-scaling or compute-allocation methods.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorem 2: under a fixed task distribution and capability preservation (nested solved-task sets), the marginal gain in solved-task probability mass tends to zero. Theorem 1 separately bounds prediction-risk increments by 2τ_n, the tail mass of a Kolmogorov-complexity prior.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For expanding systems with nested solved-task sets in a fixed task distribution, marginal gains in task coverage vanish asymptotically; no specific rate or power-law form is implied.

record.problems: The marginal-gain theorem is conditional on a fixed task distribution and capability preservation, and concerns solved-task coverage rather than empirical language-model loss. No model sweep or empirical validation of the claim versions is reported.

untested.parts: All parts: no loss measured, no parameter, token or compute sweep.
All parts: no extrapolation from small runs.
All parts: no empirical results in other modalities or regimes.
All parts: no downstream task measurements; the coverage theorem is abstract and not tied to scale or loss.
All parts: no fitted exponents or fitting choices.

record.verdict_notes: The theorem follows trivially from bounded monotone sequences. It makes no contact with power-law loss scaling and gives no rate tied to parameters, data or compute. Single-author preprint (cs.LO). No empirical content.

versions.untested_parts: All parts: held-out pretraining loss scaling with parameters, tokens, or compute.
All parts: prediction of larger-run loss from smaller-run fits.
All parts: compute-optimal parameter and token allocation.
All parts: effects of architecture details at fixed parameter count.
All parts: power-law behavior across other modalities and training regimes.
All parts: predictable downstream-task performance scaling.
All parts: dependence of fitted scaling exponents and compute-optimal allocation on setup or fitting choices, and departures from single power laws.

rows.subject: expanding generative reasoning systems
rows.operation_detail: Proves a structural result for a sequence of systems with nested solved-task sets under a fixed task distribution and capability-preservation assumption.
rows.measure: Marginal improvement in probability mass of newly solvable tasks, Δ(n).
rows.locator: Theorem 2, Section 6.4; equivalent formulation in Section 6.5
rows.note: This is a proved result about solved-task coverage, not held-out loss or a power-law fit; it does not test any listed claim version.
rows.check: This is a proved theorem (lim Δ(n)=0), not an empirical measurement of any model. The measure is solved-task coverage, not loss, and the result says nothing about power-law form. The state 'observed' is misleading; this should arguably not be a result row. It belongs under fits_no_version.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
